alerts.title: TDF-associated creatinine rise and eGFR decline
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring for patients on TDF, and list chronic kidney disease and Fanconi syndrome as major TDF toxicities. Patient's creatinine rose from 0.8 to 1.1 mg/dL and eGFR declined to 78 mL/min/1.73m² within 10 weeks of starting TDF. TDF is a likely contributor given the temporal relationship. Against drug attribution: the rise is modest, eGFR remains above 60, urinalysis is normal without proteinuria, and pregnancy itself can affect renal hemodynamics. However, the upward trend warrants close surveillance to prevent further decline.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat serum creatinine and eGFR within 3 months. If eGFR falls below 60 or creatinine continues rising, substitute TDF with ABC per guidelines.

alerts.title: Viral load timing in pregnant woman on ART
alerts.message: Guidelines state that HIV-positive pregnant women newly initiated on ART at ANC should have a VL test at 3 months on ART. This patient initiated ART 10 weeks ago (approximately 2.5 months) and already has a VL of 89 copies/mL, which is suppressed. While the result is reassuring, the timing appears slightly earlier than the 3-month guideline target. The next VL should follow the pregnant/breastfeeding algorithm: repeat at 3 months for pregnant and breastfeeding women if non-suppressed, or continue routine monitoring if suppressed.

evidence.recommended_action: Confirm VL was done per guideline schedule. Continue routine VL monitoring per pregnancy algorithm; next VL at 6 months on ART if suppressed.

alerts.title: No clinician plan documented; CPT and monitoring gaps
alerts.message: No assessment or plan was documented for this visit. Guidelines prioritize cotrimoxazole preventive therapy (CPT) for all PLHIV newly initiating on ART and for pregnant/breastfeeding women. This patient, 10 weeks into ART and pregnant, appears eligible but no CPT is listed among medications. Additionally, guidelines require HBV screening (HBsAg) for all PLHIV initiating ART; no HBV screening result is documented. TDF-containing ART is appropriate if HBV co-infected, making screening important for completeness of care.

evidence.recommended_action: Document assessment and plan. Initiate CPT if not contraindicated. Perform HBsAg screening if not yet done. Continue ferrous sulfate and folic acid.
